entries.name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
entries.definition: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of construction or extraction workers.

entries.name: Boilermakers
entries.definition: Construct, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliaries. Align structures or plate sections to assemble boiler frame tanks or vats, following blueprints. Work involves use of hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, dogs, or turnbuckles. Assist in testing assembled vessels. Direct cleaning of boilers and boiler furnaces. Inspect and repair boiler fittings, such as safety valves, regulators, automatic-control mechanisms, water columns, and auxiliary machines.

entries.name: Brickmasons and Blockmasons
entries.definition: Lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra-cotta block, with mortar and other substances, to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures. Installers of mortarless segmental concrete masonry wall units are classified in “Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers” (37-3011). Excludes “Stonemasons” (47-2022).

entries.name: Stonemasons
entries.definition: Build stone structures, such as piers, walls, and abutments. Lay walks, curbstones, or special types of masonry for vats, tanks, and floors.

entries.name: Carpenters
entries.definition: Construct, erect, install, or repair structures and fixtures made of wood and comparable materials, such as concrete forms; building frameworks, including partitions, joists, studding, and rafters; and wood stairways, window and door frames, and hardwood floors. May also install cabinets, siding, drywall, and batt or roll insulation. Includes brattice builders who build doors or brattices (ventilation walls or partitions) in underground passageways.

entries.name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Carpet Installers
entries.definition: Lay and install carpet from rolls or blocks on floors. Install padding and trim flooring materials. Excludes “Floor Layers, Except Carpet, Wood, and Hard Tiles” (47-2042).

entries.name: Floor Layers, Except Carpet, Wood, and Hard Tiles
entries.definition: Apply blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing, sound-deadening, or decorative coverings to floors.

entries.name: Floor Sanders and Finishers
entries.definition: Scrape and sand wooden floors to smooth surfaces using floor scraper and floor sanding machine, and apply coats of finish.

entries.name: Tile and Stone Setters
entries.definition: Apply hard tile, stone, and comparable materials to walls, floors, ceilings, countertops, and roof decks.

entries.name: Cement Masons, Concrete Finishers, and Terrazzo Workers
Cement Masons and Concrete Finishers
entries.definition: Smooth and finish surfaces of poured concrete, such as floors, walks, sidewalks, roads, or curbs using a variety of hand and power tools. Align forms for sidewalks, curbs, or gutters; patch voids; and use saws to cut expansion joints. Installers of mortarless segmental concrete masonry wall units are classified in “Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers” (37-3011).

entries.name: Terrazzo Workers and Finishers
entries.definition: Apply a mixture of cement, sand, pigment, or marble chips to floors, stairways, and cabinet fixtures to fashion durable and decorative surfaces.

entries.name: Construction Laborers
entries.definition: Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites. May operate hand and power tools of all types: air hammers, earth tampers, cement mixers, small mechanical hoists, surveying and measuring equipment, and a variety of other equipment and instruments. May clean and prepare sites, dig trenches, set braces to support the sides of excavations, erect scaffolding, and clean up rubble, debris, and other waste materials. May assist other craft workers. Construction laborers who primarily assist a particular craft worker are classified under “Helpers, Construction Trades” (47-3010). Excludes “Hazardous Materials Removal Workers” (47-4041).

entries.name: Paving, Surfacing, and Tamping Equipment Operators
entries.definition: Operate equipment used for applying concrete, asphalt, or other materials to road beds, parking lots, or airport runways and taxiways or for tamping gravel, dirt, or other materials. Includes concrete and asphalt paving machine operators, form tampers, tamping machine operators, and stone spreader operators.

entries.name: Pile Driver Operators
entries.definition: Operate pile drivers mounted on skids, barges, crawler treads, or locomotive cranes to drive pilings for retaining walls, bulkheads, and foundations of structures such as buildings, bridges, and piers.

entries.name: Operating Engineers and Other Construction Equipment Operators
entries.definition: Operate one or several types of power construction equipment, such as motor graders, bulldozers, scrapers, compressors, pumps, derricks, shovels, tractors, or front-end loaders to excavate, move, and grade earth, erect structures, or pour concrete or other hard surface pavement. May repair and maintain equipment in addition to other duties. Excludes “Extraction Workers” (47-5000) and “Crane and Tower Operators” (53-7021).

entries.name: Drywall Installers, Ceiling Tile Installers, and Tapers
Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers
entries.definition: Apply plasterboard or other wallboard to ceilings or interior walls of buildings. Apply or mount acoustical tiles or blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing materials to ceilings and walls of buildings to reduce or reflect sound. Materials may be of decorative quality. Includes lathers who fasten wooden, metal, or rockboard lath to walls, ceilings, or partitions of buildings to provide support base for plaster, fireproofing, or acoustical material. Excludes “Carpenters” (47-2031), “Carpet Installers” (47-2041), and “Tile and Stone Setters” (47-2044).

entries.name: Tapers
entries.definition: Seal joints between plasterboard or other wallboard to prepare wall surface for painting or papering.

entries.name: Electricians
entries.definition: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. May install or service street lights, intercom systems, or electrical control systems. Excludes “Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers” (49-2098).

entries.name: Glaziers
entries.definition: Install glass in windows, skylights, store fronts, and display cases, or on surfaces, such as building fronts, interior walls, ceilings, and tabletops.

entries.name: Insulation Workers, Floor, Ceiling, and Wall
entries.definition: Line and cover structures with insulating materials. May work with batt, roll, or blown insulation materials.

entries.name: Insulation Workers, Mechanical
entries.definition: Apply insulating materials to pipes or ductwork, or other mechanical systems in order to help control and maintain temperature.

entries.name: Painters, Construction and Maintenance
entries.definition: Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency. Excludes “Paperhangers” (47-2142).

entries.name: Paperhangers
entries.definition: Cover interior walls or ceilings of rooms with decorative wallpaper or fabric, or attach advertising posters on surfaces such as walls and billboards. May remove old materials or prepare surfaces to be papered.

entries.name: Pipelayers
entries.definition: Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, drains, and water mains. Perform any combination of the following tasks: grade trenches or culverts, position pipe, or seal joints. Excludes “Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers” (51-4121).

entries.name: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
entries.definition: Assemble, install, alter, and repair pipelines or pipe systems that carry water, steam, air, or other liquids or gases. May install heating and cooling equipment and mechanical control systems. Includes sprinkler fitters.

entries.name: Plasterers and Stucco Masons
entries.definition: Apply interior or exterior plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials. May also set ornamental plaster.

entries.name: Reinforcing Iron and Rebar Workers
entries.definition: Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms in order to reinforce concrete. Use a variety of fasteners, rod-bending machines, blowtorches, and hand tools. Includes rod busters.

entries.name: Roofers
entries.definition: Cover roofs of structures with shingles, slate, asphalt, aluminum, wood, or related materials. May spray roofs, sidings, and walls with material to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures.

entries.name: Sheet Metal Workers
entries.definition: Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair sheet metal products and equipment, such as ducts, control boxes, drainpipes, and furnace casings. Work may involve any of the following: setting up and operating fabricating machines to cut, bend, and straighten sheet metal; shaping metal over anvils, blocks, or forms using hammer; operating soldering and welding equipment to join sheet metal parts; or inspecting, assembling, and smoothing seams and joints of burred surfaces. Includes sheet metal duct installers who install prefabricated sheet metal ducts used for heating, air conditioning, or other purposes.

entries.name: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
entries.definition: Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form completed structures or structural frameworks. May erect metal storage tanks and assemble prefabricated metal buildings. Excludes “Reinforcing Iron and Rebar Workers” (47-2171).

entries.name: Solar Photovoltaic Installers
entries.definition: Assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. May include measuring, cutting, assembling, and bolting structural framing and solar modules. May perform minor electrical work such as current checks. Excludes solar PV electricians who are included in “Electricians” (47-2111) and solar thermal installers who are included in “Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters” (47-2152).

entries.name: Helpers--Brickmasons, Blockmasons, Stonemasons, and Tile and Marble Setters
entries.definition: Help brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, or tile and marble setters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist brickmasons, blockmasons, and stonemasons or tile and marble setters are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers--Carpenters
entries.definition: Help carpenters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist carpenters are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers--Electricians
entries.definition: Help electricians by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist electricians are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons
entries.definition: Help painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers--Pipelayers, Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
entries.definition: Help plumbers, pipefitters, steamfitters, or pipelayers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist plumbers, pipefitters, steamfitters, or pipelayers are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers--Roofers
entries.definition: Help roofers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment. Construction laborers who do not primarily assist roofers are classified under “Construction Laborers” (47-2061). Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Helpers, Construction Trades, All Other
entries.definition: All construction trades helpers not listed separately.

entries.name: Construction and Building Inspectors
entries.definition: Inspect structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations. Inspections may be general in nature or may be limited to a specific area, such as electrical systems or plumbing.

entries.name: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers
Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Assemble, install, repair, or maintain electric or hydraulic freight or passenger elevators, escalators, or dumbwaiters.

entries.name: Fence Erectors
entries.definition: Erect and repair fences and fence gates, using hand and power tools.

entries.name: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
entries.definition: Identify, remove, pack, transport, or dispose of hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, radioactive materials, or contaminated soil. Specialized training and certification in hazardous materials handling or a confined entry permit are generally required. May operate earth-moving equipment or trucks.

entries.name: Highway Maintenance Workers
entries.definition: Maintain highways, municipal and rural roads, airport runways, and rights-of-way. Duties include patching broken or eroded pavement and repairing guard rails, highway markers, and snow fences. May also mow or clear brush from along road, or plow snow from roadway. Excludes “Tree Trimmers and Pruners” (37-3013).

entries.name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
entries.definition: Lay, repair, and maintain track for standard or narrow-gauge railroad equipment used in regular railroad service or in plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits, and mines. Includes ballast cleaning machine operators and railroad bed tamping machine operators.

entries.name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
entries.definition: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. May patch walls and partitions of tank, replace damaged drain tile, or repair breaks in underground piping.

entries.name: Segmental Pavers
entries.definition: Lay out, cut, and place segmental paving units. Includes installers of bedding and restraining materials for the paving units.

entries.name: Construction and Related Workers, All Other
entries.definition: All construction and related workers not listed separately.

entries.name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil and Gas
Derrick Operators, Oil and Gas
entries.definition: Rig derrick equipment and operate pumps to circulate mud or fluid through drill hole.

entries.name: Rotary Drill Operators, Oil and Gas
entries.definition: Set up or operate a variety of drills to remove underground oil and gas, or remove core samples for testing during oil and gas exploration. Excludes “Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas” (47-5023).

entries.name: Service Unit Operators, Oil and Gas
entries.definition: Operate equipment to increase oil flow from producing wells or to remove stuck pipe, casing, tools, or other obstructions from drilling wells. Includes fishing-tool technicians.

entries.name: Surface Mining Machine Operators and Earth Drillers
Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators, Surface Mining
entries.definition: Operate or tend machinery at surface mining site, equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets to excavate and load loose materials.

entries.name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
entries.definition: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap subsurface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

entries.name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
entries.definition: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures.

entries.name: Continuous Mining Machine Operators
entries.definition: Operate self-propelled mining machines that rip coal, metal and nonmetal ores, rock, stone, or sand from the mine face and load it onto conveyors, shuttle cars, or trucks in a continuous operation.

entries.name: Roof Bolters, Mining
entries.definition: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.

entries.name: Loading and Moving Machine Operators, Underground Mining
entries.definition: Operate underground loading or moving machine to load or move coal, ore, or rock using shuttle or mine car or conveyors. Equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.

entries.name: Underground Mining Machine Operators, All Other
entries.definition: All underground mining machine operators not listed separately.

entries.name: Rock Splitters, Quarry
entries.definition: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammers, wedges, or chop saws.

entries.name: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
entries.definition: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.

entries.name: Helpers--Extraction Workers
entries.definition: Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area. Apprentice workers are classified with the appropriate skilled construction trade occupation (47-2011 through 47-2231).

entries.name: Extraction Workers, All Other
entries.definition: All extraction workers not listed separately.

sections.title: What distinguishes Construction and Extraction Occupations
paragraphs: The 2018 Standard Occupational Classification places Construction and Extraction Occupations in major group 47-0000. Its minor groups include Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers, Construction Trades Workers, Helpers, Construction Trades, Other Construction and Related Workers, Extraction Workers. The hierarchy then distinguishes broad occupations such as First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers, Boilermakers, Brickmasons, Blockmasons, and Stonemasons, Carpenters, Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers. Those classifications describe work performed; they do not establish an employer's exact job title, organizational seniority, professional eligibility, or a person's qualifications. Read the official definition at the level that matches the work, and compare it with the employer's written responsibilities.

The detailed records under Construction and Extraction Occupations span 61 occupations. Their definitions can help candidates and employers discuss the substance of a role when familiar titles are used differently. A useful comparison asks what outputs the person owns, which decisions they make, whom they advise or lead, and what specialized knowledge or credentials are required. A classification is a reference point, not a substitute for the job description or applicable licensing and qualification rules.

Senior positions often combine several kinds of work, while the SOC hierarchy groups occupations by their primary work concepts. A senior leader should therefore explain the actual remit in plain language: functional authority, team or stakeholder relationships, budget or service scope where disclosable, and the evidence behind claimed outcomes. Do not assume that a management title maps to one code or that an individual contributor code indicates limited organizational impact. Validate the occupation against duties and employer context.

Career transitions within Construction and Extraction Occupations should be tested against the specific minor group and detailed occupations, not just the major-group label. Compare the target duties with examples such as First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers, Boilermakers, Brickmasons, Blockmasons, and Stonemasons, Carpenters, Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers, identify the skills and outcomes that transfer, and make any gaps explicit. Where a role has a statutory credential, professional registration, clearance, or jurisdiction-specific requirement, confirm it through the employer and relevant official authority. The SOC source does not certify individual eligibility.

This page includes the complete major-group record and all 5 minor, 37 broad, and 61 detailed records. Detailed occupation definitions come from the official BLS definitions workbook; parent codes follow the BLS structure worksheet sequence rather than an assumed code-prefix rule. This makes the table traceable to both source workbooks and helps distinguish similar titles whose work concepts differ.

For international career planning, map the duties to the relevant local occupational classification rather than assuming that a U.S. SOC code translates directly. Compare the employing entity, target role, actual responsibility, location, work authorization, and credential requirements. Current market evidence should be dated and sourced to official statistics or employer disclosures. The table is not a demand or salary ranking and does not claim that one country has more opportunities than another.

Depending on the written engagement, support may help define target roles, organize evidence, research organizations, and coordinate applications or outreach approved by the professional. Candidates retain approval of external activity; employers retain hiring decisions. Scope, deliverables, fees, and reporting are agreed directly before work begins. No interview, offer, employment outcome, or timing is guaranteed.

Record credential questions separately for confirmation with the employer or relevant authority. This makes the classification useful as a research aid without presenting it as proof of an individual's experience or professional eligibility.

Use major group 47-0000 as the beginning of a role comparison, then move through the official hierarchy until the specific work concept is relevant. When a position spans several specialties, document the primary duties and the additional responsibilities rather than selecting a code from the title alone. entries.name: Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
entries.definition: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of mechanics, installers, and repairers. May also advise customers on recommended services. Excludes team or work leaders.

entries.name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
entries.definition: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

entries.name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Repair, install, or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems used in cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, and radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles. May test and analyze network coverage.

entries.name: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
entries.definition: Install, set up, rearrange, or remove switching, distribution, routing, and dialing equipment used in central offices or headends. Service or repair telephone, cable television, Internet, and other communications equipment on customers’ property. May install communications equipment or communications wiring in buildings. Excludes “Telecommunications Line Installers and Repairers” (49-9052).

entries.name: Miscellaneous Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Avionics Technicians
entries.definition: Install, inspect, test, adjust, or repair avionics equipment, such as radar, radio, navigation, and missile control systems in aircraft or space vehicles.

entries.name: Electric Motor, Power Tool, and Related Repairers
entries.definition: Repair, maintain, or install electric motors, wiring, or switches.

entries.name: Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment
entries.definition: Install, adjust, or maintain mobile electronics communication equipment, including sound, sonar, security, navigation, and surveillance systems on trains, watercraft, or other mobile equipment. Excludes “Avionics Technicians” (49-2091) and “Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles” (49-2096).

entries.name: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
entries.definition: Repair, test, adjust, or install electronic equipment, such as industrial controls, transmitters, and antennas. Excludes “Avionics Technicians” (49-2091), “Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment” (49-2093), and “Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles” (49-2096).

entries.name: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay
entries.definition: Inspect, test, repair, or maintain electrical equipment in generating stations, substations, and in-service relays.

entries.name: Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles
entries.definition: Install, diagnose, or repair communications, sound, security, or navigation equipment in motor vehicles.

entries.name: Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Install, repair, or adjust audio or television receivers, stereo systems, camcorders, video systems, or other electronic entertainment equipment in homes or other venues. May perform routine maintenance. Excludes “Audio and Video Technicians” (27-4011).

entries.name: Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers
entries.definition: Install, program, maintain, and repair security and fire alarm wiring and equipment. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. Excludes “Electricians” (47-2111) who do a broad range of electrical wiring.

entries.name: Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Excludes “Avionics Technicians” (49-2091).

entries.name: Automotive Body and Related Repairers
entries.definition: Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames. Excludes “Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers” (49-3022) and “Coating, Painting, and Spraying Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders” (51-9124).

entries.name: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Replace or repair broken windshields and window glass in motor vehicles.

entries.name: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul automotive vehicles. Excludes “Automotive Body and Related Repairers” (49-3021), “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031), and “Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles” (49-2096).

entries.name: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul buses and trucks, or maintain and repair any type of diesel engines. Includes mechanics working primarily with automobile or marine diesel engines.

entries.name: Heavy Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Service Technicians and Mechanics
Farm Equipment Mechanics and Service Technicians
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, dairy equipment, and irrigation systems. Excludes “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031).

entries.name: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, graders, and conveyors, used in construction, logging, and mining. Excludes “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031) and “Rail Car Repairers” (49-3043).

entries.name: Rail Car Repairers
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul railroad rolling stock, mine cars, or mass transit rail cars. Excludes “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031).

entries.name: Motorboat Mechanics and Service Technicians
entries.definition: Repair and adjust electrical and mechanical equipment of inboard or inboard-outboard boat engines. Excludes “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031).

entries.name: Motorcycle Mechanics
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, dirt bikes, or similar motorized vehicles.

entries.name: Outdoor Power Equipment and Other Small Engine Mechanics
entries.definition: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul small engines used to power lawn mowers, chain saws, recreational sporting equipment, and related equipment.

entries.name: Miscellaneous Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Bicycle Repairers
entries.definition: Repair and service bicycles.

entries.name: Recreational Vehicle Service Technicians
entries.definition: Diagnose, inspect, adjust, repair, or overhaul recreational vehicles including travel trailers. May specialize in maintaining gas, electrical, hydraulic, plumbing, or chassis/towing systems as well as repairing generators, appliances, and interior components. Includes workers who perform customized van conversions. Excludes “Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics” (49-3023) and “Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists” (49-3031) who also work on recreation vehicles.

entries.name: Tire Repairers and Changers
entries.definition: Repair and replace tires.

entries.name: Other Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations
Control and Valve Installers and Repairers
Mechanical Door Repairers
entries.definition: Install, service, or repair automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors. Includes garage door mechanics.

entries.name: Control and Valve Installers and Repairers, Except Mechanical Door
entries.definition: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical regulating and controlling devices, such as electric meters, gas regulators, thermostats, safety and flow valves, and other mechanical governors.

entries.name: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
entries.definition: Install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC, or refrigeration systems, including oil burners, hot-air furnaces, and heating stoves.

entries.name: Home Appliance Repairers
entries.definition: Repair, adjust, or install all types of electric or gas household appliances, such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, and ovens.

entries.name: Industrial Machinery Installation, Repair, and Maintenance Workers
Industrial Machinery Mechanics
entries.definition: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Excludes “Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines” (49-3042), and “Maintenance Workers, Machinery” (49-9043).

entries.name: Maintenance Workers, Machinery
entries.definition: Lubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance. Excludes “Maintenance and Repair Workers, General” (49-9071).

entries.name: Millwrights
entries.definition: Install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to layout plans, blueprints, or other drawings.

entries.name: Refractory Materials Repairers, Except Brickmasons
entries.definition: Build or repair equipment such as furnaces, kilns, cupolas, boilers, converters, ladles, soaking pits, and ovens, using refractory materials.

entries.name: Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Install or repair cables or wires used in electrical power or distribution systems. May erect poles and light or heavy duty transmission towers. Excludes “Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay” (49-2095).

entries.name: Telecommunications Line Installers and Repairers
entries.definition: Install and repair telecommunications cable, including fiber optics.

entries.name: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
entries.definition: Repair and adjust cameras and photographic equipment, including commercial video and motion picture camera equipment.

entries.name: Medical Equipment Repairers
entries.definition: Test, adjust, or repair biomedical or electromedical equipment.

entries.name: Musical Instrument Repairers and Tuners
entries.definition: Repair percussion, stringed, reed, or wind instruments. May specialize in one area, such as piano tuning. Excludes “Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers" (49-2097) who repair electrical and electronic musical instruments.

entries.name: Watch and Clock Repairers
entries.definition: Repair, clean, and adjust mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks. Includes watchmakers, watch technicians, and mechanical timepiece repairers. Excludes "Timing Device Assemblers and Adjusters” (51-2061).

entries.name: Precision Instrument and Equipment Repairers, All Other
entries.definition: All precision instrument and equipment repairers not listed separately.

entries.name: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
entries.definition: Perform work involving the skills of two or more maintenance or craft occupations to keep machines, mechanical equipment, or the structure of a building in repair. Duties may involve pipe fitting; HVAC maintenance; insulating; welding; machining; carpentry; repairing electrical or mechanical equipment; installing, aligning, and balancing new equipment; and repairing buildings, floors, or stairs. Excludes “Facilities Managers” (11-3013) and “Maintenance Workers, Machinery” (49-9043).

entries.name: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
entries.definition: Inspect, diagnose, adjust, or repair wind turbines. Perform maintenance on wind turbine equipment including resolving electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic malfunctions.

entries.name: Miscellaneous Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
Coin, Vending, and Amusement Machine Servicers and Repairers
entries.definition: Install, service, adjust, or repair coin, vending, or amusement machines including video games, juke boxes, pinball machines, or slot machines.

entries.name: Commercial Divers
entries.definition: Work below surface of water, using surface-supplied air or scuba equipment to inspect, repair, remove, or install equipment and structures. May use a variety of power and hand tools, such as drills, sledgehammers, torches, and welding equipment. May conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, or photograph structures or marine life. Excludes “Athletes and Sports Competitors” (27-2021), “Police and Sheriff’s Patrol Officers” (33-3051), and “Fishing and Hunting Workers” (45-3031).

entries.name: Locksmiths and Safe Repairers
entries.definition: Repair and open locks, make keys, change locks and safe combinations, and install and repair safes.

entries.name: Manufactured Building and Mobile Home Installers
entries.definition: Move or install mobile homes or prefabricated buildings.

entries.name: Riggers
entries.definition: Set up or repair rigging for construction projects, manufacturing plants, logging yards, ships and shipyards, or for the entertainment industry.

entries.name: Signal and Track Switch Repairers
entries.definition: Install, inspect, test, maintain, or repair electric gate crossings, signals, signal equipment, track switches, section lines, or intercommunications systems within a railroad system.

entries.name: Helpers--Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
entries.definition: Help installation, maintenance, and repair workers in maintenance, parts replacement, and repair of vehicles, industrial machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment. Perform duties such as furnishing tools, materials, and supplies to other workers; cleaning work area, machines, and tools; and holding materials or tools for other workers.

entries.name: Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other
entries.definition: All installation, maintenance, and repair workers not listed separately.

sections.title: What distinguishes Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations
paragraphs: The 2018 Standard Occupational Classification places Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations in major group 49-0000. Its minor groups include Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Other Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations. The hierarchy then distinguishes broad occupations such as First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers, Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Miscellaneous Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians. Those classifications describe work performed; they do not establish an employer's exact job title, organizational seniority, professional eligibility, or a person's qualifications. Read the official definition at the level that matches the work, and compare it with the employer's written responsibilities.

The detailed records under Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations span 51 occupations. Their definitions can help candidates and employers discuss the substance of a role when familiar titles are used differently. A useful comparison asks what outputs the person owns, which decisions they make, whom they advise or lead, and what specialized knowledge or credentials are required. A classification is a reference point, not a substitute for the job description or applicable licensing and qualification rules.

Senior positions often combine several kinds of work, while the SOC hierarchy groups occupations by their primary work concepts. A senior leader should therefore explain the actual remit in plain language: functional authority, team or stakeholder relationships, budget or service scope where disclosable, and the evidence behind claimed outcomes. Do not assume that a management title maps to one code or that an individual contributor code indicates limited organizational impact. Validate the occupation against duties and employer context.

Career transitions within Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations should be tested against the specific minor group and detailed occupations, not just the major-group label. Compare the target duties with examples such as First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers, Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Miscellaneous Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers, Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians, identify the skills and outcomes that transfer, and make any gaps explicit. Where a role has a statutory credential, professional registration, clearance, or jurisdiction-specific requirement, confirm it through the employer and relevant official authority. The SOC source does not certify individual eligibility.

This page includes the complete major-group record and all 4 minor, 19 broad, and 51 detailed records. Detailed occupation definitions come from the official BLS definitions workbook; parent codes follow the BLS structure worksheet sequence rather than an assumed code-prefix rule. This makes the table traceable to both source workbooks and helps distinguish similar titles whose work concepts differ.

For international career planning, map the duties to the relevant local occupational classification rather than assuming that a U.S. SOC code translates directly. Compare the employing entity, target role, actual responsibility, location, work authorization, and credential requirements. Current market evidence should be dated and sourced to official statistics or employer disclosures. The table is not a demand or salary ranking and does not claim that one country has more opportunities than another.

KOV Career Agency provides candidate-side career representation and individual career services. Depending on the written engagement, support may help define target roles, organize evidence, research organizations, and coordinate applications or outreach approved by the professional. Candidates retain approval of external activity; employers retain hiring decisions. Scope, deliverables, fees, and reporting are agreed directly before work begins. No interview, offer, employment outcome, or timing is guaranteed.

For a practical Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations search, keep the target job description beside the relevant official definitions and note where the duties agree or differ. Record credential questions separately for confirmation with the employer or relevant authority. This makes the classification useful as a research aid without presenting it as proof of an individual's experience or professional eligibility.

Use major group 49-0000 as the beginning of a role comparison, then move through the official hierarchy until the specific work concept is relevant. When a position spans several specialties, document the primary duties and the additional responsibilities rather than selecting a code from the title alone. This distinction is particularly useful in executive searches, where titles can be broad and authority varies widely. A written comparison keeps the discussion grounded in the work, the evidence, and the requirements confirmed with the prospective employer.
